message.content:
In standard Blackjack, an Ace is a “flexible” card: it can be worth **either 1 or 11 points**, whichever gives the hand the best possible total without busting.

**Key points**

| Situation | How the Ace is counted |
|-----------|------------------------|
| **Single Ace** | You choose 1 or 11. If counting it as 11 would make the hand exceed 21, you automatically count it as 1. |
| **Two Aces** | One Ace is counted as 11 and the other as 1 (so the hand totals 12). If you had three Aces, you’d count one as 11 and the others as 1, etc. |
| **Ace + 10‑value card (10, J, Q, K)** | This is a “Blackjack” (natural 21). The Ace counts as 11. |
| **After a split** | If you split Aces, most casinos allow only one additional card per Ace and the Ace remains valued at 11 for that new hand. |

So, the rule is simply: **An Ace can be 1 or 11, whichever benefits the hand, but it will never be forced to 11 if that would bust the hand.**
